newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes just up but downtrend prevails.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes just up but downtrend prevails.

text.p: Some physical buying of gold helped support precious metals prices on Wednesday but there were few factors around to suggest anything other than a day of narrow range trading, dealers said.
"There is good support from reasonable physical offtake but producer selling is expected on any sort of rally," a dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $338.70 per ounce up from $338.35 on Tuesday afternoon when prices came under pressure from a reviving U.S. stock market and firmer dollar.

Gold had rallied on Tuesday after overnight comments by the Japanese prime minister -- later said to be misinterpreted -- had suggested Japan would consider selling its reserves of U.S. Treasury bonds and buying gold.
But dealers said there was insufficient follow-through buying to sustain the move after the resultant chaos in the U.S. financial markets settled on Tuesday.
"Gold is on a torturous journey. There is nothing to suggest it will pick up unless there is a collapse in the stock markets or something completely unforeseen," one dealer said.
Little change was forecast for prices today with the market holding in an outside range of $337.00-$340.00, dealers said.
Hopes that interest in silver could lead the complex to higher ground began to crumble Tuesday afternoon when it failed to build on a move to around $4.80.
Silver has failed there three times recently and needed to get through $4.85 to encourage further buying, dealers said.
"There is still probably more potential in silver than gold," one dealer said, adding that it was silver which started the move higher earlier this week.
It was indicated at an unchanged $4.77/$4.79 at 0945 GMT.
Platinum was virtually unchanged as well at $412.00/$417.00 in a nervous and tight market.
The price has come off from its seven-year high fixing of $495.00 struck on June 6 reflecting the market largely abandoning forward positions due to its severe tightness.
Palladium has also come off highs -- a 17-year peak of $240.00 on June 6 -- as its tightness also strangled forward dealing. It was indicated at $192.00/$197.00 down $3.00.

Russia the largest palladium exporter and second largest supplier of platinum has not exported metal since December due to administrative problems but is due to resume exports to Japan, its biggest customer, next month. Meanwhile the market will be cautious, dealers said.
